correctness.rationale: For q>=3, at most one positive per q-clique fiber and no empty fiber because two neighbors cannot defend q rows. A label-one fiber requires q<=3; for q=3 its two adjacent two-label colors must be distinct and complementary. Thus S={one-label fibers} is independent and the weight is 2n-|S|. Maximum independent sets on an even/odd cycle and proper colorings of cyclic lists give both the optimum and exact counts, including explicit small-list cases n=3,4. The package verifier exhaustively checks 13 layer encodings and 7 independently built graph instances; infinite scope follows from proof, not computation.

The theorem identifies a sharp change from flexible ternary 1/2 defenses to rigid all-two defenses, explicitly classifies all optimal assignments, and gives closed multiplicity formulas via proper cyclic colorings. These give information beyond numerical optimization for an unbounded two-parameter family.
